surprises.description: Adjusted EPS was $1.03, above the preview’s operative $0.95–$1.00 bar. The beat was modest, though adjusted PPNR came in below the preview’s build.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Q3 2026 adjusted net income was $48.2 million, or $1.03 per diluted share,” excluding $0.21 per share of after-tax merger expenses.

surprises.description: NIM expanded to 3.82%, ahead of the preview’s 3.78% base case and above the 3.76% June exit rate. This was a favorable but relatively narrow gap; the Q4 outlook remained in the expected mid-3.80s.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest margin expanded 24 basis points to 3.82% in Q3 from 3.58% in Q2, with Q4 guidance in the mid-3.80s.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview modeled Q3 NIM at “3.78%” and said “NIM at or above 3.78% keeps the bridge intact.”

surprises.description: Adjusted PPNR was weaker than the preview’s base build: Q3 was $1.42 per share, while the preview modeled about $72 million of adjusted PPNR, roughly $1.56 per share using its 46.2 million share assumption. This contrasts with the EPS beat and reflects a weaker underlying pre-provision result than expected.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted PPNR was $1.42 per share in Q3, down from $1.50 in Q2.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base-case build listed “Adj. PPNR” at “~$72M.”

surprises.description: Credit results were somewhat better than the expected mid-teens-basis-point H2 charge-off level: Q3 net charge-offs were 11 basis points annualized, while special mention and substandard loans both declined. This was favorable evidence on the credit concerns highlighted in the preview.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Special mention loans down ~$23.8 million and substandard loans down ~$39.9 million,” with “net charge-offs … $3.3 million (11 basis points annualized).”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said management guided H2 net charge-offs to the “mid-teens” bps and flagged that NPAs needed to stop rising.

surprises.description: Loan performance and the Q4 outlook fell short of the preview’s anticipated growth pace: total loans declined 3.8% annualized in Q3, and management guided to only mid-single-digit Q4 growth rather than the preview’s low-double-digit annualized H2 guide. Higher pipelines and C&I production provide some offset, but paydowns in other portfolios outweighed them.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total loan balances declined ~$110 million (3.8% annualized),” as C&I growth was “more than offset” by paydowns; management guided to “mid-single-digit Q4 loan … growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview identified a “low double-digit annualized” H2 loan-growth guide and modeled a base case of “high-single-digit rather than low-double” growth.

surprises.description: The company repurchased more shares in Q3 than the preview expected, buying about $50 million against an anticipated $35–40 million. Management also expects to finish the remaining $100 million over the next three quarters, maintaining a clear execution timetable for the authorization.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The company repurchased approximately $50 million of common shares in Q3” and “expects to complete the remaining $100 million over the next three quarters.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview said to “expect ~$35–40M” in Q3 and described the $150 million authorization as being executed over four quarters.

surprises.description: Tangible book value per share reached $35.60, below the preview’s expected $35.80–$36.30 range despite retained earnings and the buyback. The shortfall was modest, but the anticipated degree of TBVPS accretion did not materialize.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Tangible book value per share increased to $35.60 from $35.16 despite the $50 million buyback.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview expected TBVPS “to still accrete to roughly $35.8–36.3 on retained earnings.”

surprises.description: Deposits fell by about $447 million, a significant decline not quantified in the preview. The explanation tempers the concern: roughly 80% was described as intentional runoff or seasonal contraction, and management guided to mid-single-digit Q4 deposit growth excluding brokered deposits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Total deposits fell ~$447 million, with roughly 80% from intentional runoff or seasonal contraction,” including higher-rate non-relationship balances and brokered deposits.
